label: Perfect Simple
desc: Completed actions, life experience, unfinished time periods

items.after: each other for five years now.
items.note: 'know' is a state verb; use Present Perfect Simple with 'for' — the period is unfinished, so not Past Simple.
Life experience up to now → Present Perfect, not Past Simple.

items.after: her homework, so she can go out now.
items.note: 'just' with a result visible now → Present Perfect, not Past Simple.
'since' + a period continuing to now → Present Perfect, not Past Simple.
A life-experience question → Present Perfect ('Have you ever...?'), not Past Simple.

items.after: his passport, so he can't travel.
items.note: A past action with a present result (he can't travel now) → Present Perfect Simple.

items.after: that book already, so I don't need to buy it.
items.note: 'already' with a present consequence → Present Perfect Simple.
'yet' in a negative about the present → Present Perfect Simple, not Past Simple.
'in your life' asks about experience up to now → Present Perfect Simple.
'since' + an unfinished period → Present Perfect Simple.

label: Perfect Continuous
desc: Ongoing duration and recent activity with visible results

items.after: English for three years, and I still have a lot to learn.
items.note: Duration continuing up to now → Present Perfect Continuous, not the simple form.
Recent activity explaining a present result → Present Perfect Continuous.
'How long' about something still in progress → Present Perfect Continuous.
'since' + duration still continuing → Present Perfect Continuous.
Duration explaining a present physical result → Present Perfect Continuous.

items.after: all day, so the roads are very wet.
items.note: Ongoing activity with visible present evidence → Present Perfect Continuous.
Repeated action over a period up to now → Present Perfect Continuous.
Temporary ongoing situation since a past point → Present Perfect Continuous.
Duration up to now explaining a present state → Present Perfect Continuous.
'How long' + an activity still ongoing → Present Perfect Continuous.

label: Past Perfect
desc: The earlier of two past events

items.cue: When I arrived at the cinema, the film
items.note: The earlier of two past actions → Past Perfect, not Past Simple.
The cause happened even earlier in the past → Past Perfect.

items.after: snow before I moved to Canada.
items.note: Experience before another past point → Past Perfect.

items.cue: By the time we arrived, they
items.note: Completed before another past moment → Past Perfect.
The earlier action in a past sequence → Past Perfect.

items.cue: The house was dirty because nobody
items.note: Explaining a past state with an even-earlier past action → Past Perfect.

items.after: at all, so he failed the exam.
items.note: The earlier cause of a later past result → Past Perfect.
An earlier past event explaining a later one → Past Perfect.

items.cue: When he woke up, he realized he
items.note: The earlier past action, discovered later → Past Perfect.

items.after: at the company for ten years.
items.note: 'By' + a past deadline, with a period completed before it → Past Perfect.
Duration leading up to a past result → Past Perfect Continuous.

items.cue: The ground was wet because it
items.note: Visible past evidence, explained by duration → Past Perfect Continuous.
A recently finished activity with visible past evidence → Past Perfect Continuous.
Duration before a past state → Past Perfect Continuous.
'How long' about duration up to a past moment → Past Perfect Continuous.
Duration explaining a past physical result → Past Perfect Continuous.

items.cue: He knew London well because he
items.note: An ongoing situation explaining a past state → Past Perfect Continuous.

items.cue: The roads were icy because it
items.note: Duration explaining visible past evidence → Past Perfect Continuous.

items.cue: She failed her test because she
items.note: Repeated lack of activity before a past result → Past Perfect Continuous.
Duration up to a specific past moment → Past Perfect Continuous.

label: Future Forms
desc: Will, going to, and present forms for the future

items.cue: Look at those dark clouds! It
items.note: A prediction with present evidence → 'going to'.
An opinion-based prediction, no visible evidence → 'will'.
A fixed personal arrangement with time and place set → Present Continuous.
A decided plan → 'going to', not 'will'.
A decision made at the moment of speaking → 'will'.
A prediction based on what you can see right now → 'going to'.
A fixed timetable → Present Simple.

items.after: late, so don't wait for me.
items.note: An opinion-based prediction with an adverb → 'will'.

items.after: to New York next Friday for a conference.
items.note: A fixed, booked arrangement → Present Continuous.
A decision made on the spot → 'will'.

label: Narrative Tenses
desc: Telling a story: simple, continuous and perfect together

items.after: home, I saw an old friend.
items.note: A longer background action interrupted by a shorter one → Past Continuous.

items.cue: When the police arrived, the thieves
items.note: The earlier of two past actions → Past Perfect.

items.after: a book when the doorbell rang.
items.note: Background action in progress, interrupted by a shorter one → Past Continuous.

items.after: before my trip to Spain last year.
items.note: Experience before another past point → Past Perfect.

items.after: the news, I called my parents.
items.note: A short, complete past action → Past Simple.

items.after: heavily when we left the restaurant.
items.note: Background action in progress at a past moment → Past Continuous.

items.after: his studies, he moved to London.
items.note: The earlier action in a past sequence → Past Perfect.

items.after: in the garden when it started to snow.
items.note: Background action already in progress → Past Continuous.

items.cue: By the time I woke up, everyone
items.note: Completed before another past moment → Past Perfect.

items.after: dinner, her husband set the table.
items.note: Two actions happening at the same time in the past → Past Continuous for both.

label: Present Contrast
desc: Simple vs continuous — habits/facts vs temporary situations

items.cue: I usually drive to work, but today I
items.note: A one-off change from a routine → Present Continuous, not Present Simple.

items.after: with her parents temporarily while she looks for a flat.
items.note: A temporary situation, not a permanent one → Present Continuous.
A permanent scientific fact → Present Simple.
Happening at the exact moment of speaking → Present Continuous.
'understand' is a state verb — Present Simple, never continuous.

items.after: on a special project this month.
items.note: A temporary activity around now → Present Continuous.
A permanent, timeless fact → Present Simple.

items.after: a suit today? You usually wear jeans.
items.note: A one-off change from the usual → Present Continuous.
A fixed timetable → Present Simple, even with a future time word.

items.after: to concentrate, so please be quiet!
items.note: Happening at this exact moment → Present Continuous.

label: Mixed Advanced
desc: Every tense mixed — the full C1 test

items.after: in this house for ten years.
items.note: Future Perfect for a state whose duration reaches into the future.
Duration continuing up to now → Present Perfect Continuous.
Reported speech shifts the tense one step back → Past Perfect.

items.after: the train if we don't hurry!
items.note: A prediction based on present evidence (the time) → 'going to'.

items.after: that film three times already, but I'd watch it again.
items.note: Experience up to now, counted with 'times' → Present Perfect.

items.after: the car, he cut his finger.
items.note: Background action interrupted by a short one → Past Continuous.

items.cue: Don't call me between 8 and 9 tomorrow. I
items.note: In progress at a specific future time → Future Continuous.

items.cue: I can't find my keys. I
items.note: A past action with a present result → Present Perfect.
A fixed schedule → Present Simple.

items.cue: By the time you read this, I
items.note: Completed before a future reference point → Future Perfect.
